newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica opens bidding for crude exploration.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica opens bidding for crude exploration.

text.p: Costa Rica has opened up crude oil exploration rights for bidding by domestic and foreign companies, Energy and Environment minister Rene Castro told reporters Thursday.
Castro said the concessions will require investments of between $10 million and $50 million.
Foreign and national companies will have equal access to the bidding process, he said.
The exploration rights will last three years each for 10 offshore sites and 15 land regions.
Crude exploration in Costa Rica began in 1915 and was suspended in 1988. No significant reserves of petroleum were ever found.
